coordination_notes: rapid, synchronized middle leg extension, wing depression and flight initiation (single movement)
mapping_basis: Paper names the neuron GF and states it is also known as DNp01; synonyms.csv maps GF uniquely to DNp01 (not ambiguous).
notes: Driver called 'GF-split-Gal4' in the paper (Table 1: R17A04-p65ADZp (attP40); R68A06-ZpGdbd (attP2)), described as 'highly specific', cites von Reyn 2014. Escape scored by eye from slow-motion smartphone video (simulated 1000 fps); only takeoff scored, legs coded 'no' per single-movement convention. Each fly stimulated once.
penetrance: about 83% of retinal-fed GF>CsChrimson flies escaped (bar height read from Fig 2B); 0% in all three controls
quote: We found that only flies that expressed CsChrimson in the GF and had been fed retinal displayed takeoff behaviors (Fig 2B and S1 Movie).
sensory_condition: tethered on tungsten wire, holding a small piece of Kimwipe; dark-recovered
source_locator: Fig 2A-B; Results 'Device validation–activating escape neurons'; S1 Movie (not downloaded)
stimulation: 627 nm red LED, 0.16 mW/mm2 at the fly, single 300 ms pulse; flies fed all-trans-retinal
title: An optogenetics device with smartphone video capture to introduce neurotechnology and systems neuroscience to high school students.

coordination_notes: complete interruption of appendage movement (>=120 ms absence of leg motion) during and after light, then leg movement resumes
mapping_basis: Paper names DNp09 (Namiki nomenclature, line cited to Namiki 2018) for SS1540; the kit lists DNp09 as ambiguous (DNp09;DNp71 via hemibrain name), Namiki usage supports MANC DNp09.
n_flies_note: 80 retinal-fed experimental flies; 79 non-retinal SS1540>CsChrimson; 24 per WT control (Fig 3B)
notes: Paper writes the line as 'SS1540-split-Gal4' (Table 1: VT023490-p65ADZp (attP40); R38F04-ZpGAL4DBD (attP2)); kit ID SS01540. Paper states the exact freezing neurons are unknown and that DNp09 may instead drive forward locomotion; the authors did not observe increased locomotion, attributing this to tethered flies lacking tarsal contact. Fly was not walking (tethered, moving legs via grooming/struggling); 'stops' codes cessation of that leg movement. Scored by eye by a non-blinded experimenter.
other_cell_types: unidentified other neurons labelled by SS1540-split-Gal4 (paper, citing Bidaye et al. 2020, suggests these cause freezing)
penetrance: about 62% of retinal-fed SS1540>CsChrimson flies froze (bar height read from Fig 3B); about 20% of non-retinal SS1540>CsChrimson flies also froze; 0% in WT controls
quote: We found that flies expressing CsChrimson in neurons labeled by this line displayed freezing behavior at a high probability (Fig 3A, 3B and S2 Movie).
sensory_condition: tethered on tungsten wire, no substrate (no tarsal contact); flies given/removed Kimwipe to induce an active leg-moving state; dark-recovered
source_locator: Fig 3A-B; Results 'Device validation–activating freezing neurons'; S2 Movie (not downloaded)
stimulation: 627 nm red LED, 0.16 mW/mm2 at the fly, single 300 ms pulse; flies fed all-trans-retinal
title: An optogenetics device with smartphone video capture to introduce neurotechnology and systems neuroscience to high school students.
